fatal_errors: The proposed method is an annealing experiment, whereas the target method is molecular-dynamics simulation of uniaxial tension along selected crystallographic orientations.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as an as-cast polycrystalline alloy rather than a single-crystal FCC equiatomic FeNiCrMn model.
The hypothesis omits the central variables of crystallographic orientation, tensile strain rate, and testing temperature.
The proposed grain-growth and precipitation mechanism does not match the target mechanism involving vacancy-assisted nucleation of Shockley partial dislocations and stacking faults.
The quantitative improvements in strength and ductility are unsupported by evidence and are not target outcomes.
explanation: The response only broadly addresses mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn. It reconstructs neither the molecular-dynamics tensile method nor its rationale: MD enables atomistic examination of orientation, temperature, and strain-rate effects and identification of dislocations and stacking faults through DXA/CNA. The annealing design is experimentally testable, but its temperature range, microstructural mediators, numerical predictions, and falsification thresholds are arbitrary and uncited. It also misses the reported anisotropic yield response, temperature-induced softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, increased dislocation density at higher rates, and absence of BCC transformation or twinning.
